transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you here today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm in the right place, I just... I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in. It's a little embarrassing to talk about, honestly, so please tell me if I'm not explaining this right. 

But, um... well, if I end up eating a bit too much, I've been... going to the bathroom and sort of making myself sick? Like, making myself throw up. I just really don't want to gain weight, you know? I know it's a bad habit, and I really do try to take care of myself, but it's gotten to the point where I'm actually a little scared that I can't stop doing it. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I brought that up.

Can you tell me more about when you make yourself sick after eating — does it usually happen after you’ve eaten a larger amount of food than most people would in one sitting, or does it happen even after eating just a normal or small amount?

Um... well, I guess... I hope you don't think terribly of me for saying this, but it's usually a larger amount. I really try to be good during the day, I promise I do. But... sometimes at night, after everyone’s gone quiet and I'm just by myself... I’ll just stand in the kitchen and start eating. 

I'll have leftovers, and then maybe some cereal, chips, ice cream... just whatever’s there, really. I don't even sit down half the time. I just keep going way past what a normal meal would be, until... well, until half the pantry looks picked over. I know it's a terrible habit, I'm so sorry. It sounds so bad when I say it out loud. Is that... is that the kind of information you needed? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.

How often do you make yourself sick after eating — is this something that happens most days, a few times a week, or less often? Also, do you do anything else to try to control your weight, like skipping meals, exercising a lot, or using laxatives?

Um... well, I hope this doesn't sound too awful... but it's been happening pretty regularly. For at least the past three months, honestly, there’s hardly been a single week where I didn’t have one of those late-night eating things and then... you know, go to the bathroom to make myself sick afterward. Some weeks it happens several times, especially lately. I've been home a lot more because I hurt my back at the shop—I'm a mechanic, so it's a lot of heavy lifting—and being stuck at home just makes it harder to resist, I guess. 

As for the other things... I don't use laxatives or anything like that, I promise. And I can't really exercise much right now because of my back. I do try to skip breakfast or lunch sometimes, just to balance things out, you know? To try and be good. I really am trying my best to handle it. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.
When you're eating during these late-night episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating once you start?

Um... yeah, I guess that's exactly how it feels. I hope it doesn't make me sound completely crazy, but... once I start on those nights, it’s like my hands just keep grabbing food. Even while I’m standing there literally telling myself, 'Lucy, knock it off, you don't need this,' it's like I just can't listen to myself. 

I don’t really feel back in charge of things until it’s already done and the food is gone. I know I should be stronger than that, and I really do try to just stop, I promise. It's just... in the moment, it feels like I can't. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too... out of control. I really am trying to keep it together.
Do you usually make yourself vomit after these late-night eating episodes, or does it only happen occasionally?

Um... gosh, I really wish I could tell you it was just every once in a while. I don't want you to think terribly of me... but, well, it’s pretty much every time. 

Like I mentioned before about going to the bathroom... after I eat too much on those nights, I just panic. I keep making myself throw up because I'm just so terrified I'll gain weight from all that food. I really do try to fight it, I promise I do, but... honestly, it’s gotten to the point where I’m scared I can’t stop doing it. 

I know it's an awful thing to do, and I'm so sorry. I hope you aren't too disappointed in me for letting it get this bad. Is... is that what you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Can you tell me how you feel about your body or your weight? Does it affect how you see yourself or how you feel about who you are?

Um... well, I hope this doesn't sound too vain or silly for someone my age... but my weight is kind of all I think about sometimes. I really try not to let it bother me, I promise I do, but... it just does. 

Like, if I put on my work pants and they feel even a little bit tight, or if I just happen to catch a glimpse of my belly in the mirror... it just ruins everything. I instantly feel like I'm failing. Like I'm just this weak person, and not the strong woman who used to be able to yank out transmissions and keep up with all the guys at the shop. It makes me feel like I'm losing the only part of myself I was actually proud of. 

I know I shouldn't let my body dictate how I feel about myself as a person, and I'm really trying to be better about it. I hope that doesn't make me sound too superficial or anything? I just want to be honest with you so you can help me fix it.
Would you say that your overall sense of how you feel about yourself is very much connected to how you feel about your weight or shape?

Um... yes, I guess it really is. I hope you don't think I'm just repeating myself, but... yeah, they're definitely connected. 

Like I was saying before, it just takes something so small... like if my work pants feel a little tight, or if I just happen to catch sight of my belly in the mirror... and it just, I don't know, it makes me feel like I'm failing at everything. It's like I'm not that strong woman anymore, the one who used to be able to handle transmissions and keep up with all the guys at the shop. It just feels like if my body isn't right, then I'm not right. 

I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself, and I really am trying to look at the bigger picture. I hope it's okay that I feel this way... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you.
